_about: The Improve obligation ledger (ShipLoop efficiency plan U18): one row per paragraph or list item of the four sources the Improve card's ShipLoop route replaces (skills/improve/SKILL.md as it stood before the split, references/review-policy.md, references/callback-evidence.md, runtime/until-loop/ADAPTER.md), and of the new text. `file` and `head` (the first five words, whitespace-normalized) say where the source block stands now: SKILL.md (the router, which a ShipLoop child loads), standalone-route.md (the five standalone sections moved whole, text unchanged but for three links) or its own file. `route` is a phrase of references/shiploop-route.md that carries the obligation for a ShipLoop child; a row with no `route` phrase and not in the router names why in `reason` (standalone-only, illustrative, or covered by another row). test/improve-route.test.py fails when a block of those files has no row, when a `head` or `route` phrase is gone, or when a row has neither a phrase, nor a reason, nor a place in the router. A unit that moves an obligation changes its row in the same commit. Since 2026-10-24 the route is a core (shiploop-route.md, what every child reads) and five case files the core names with the case that opens them; a `route` phrase may stand in any of them. A row whose phrase stands only in the long form (shiploop-route-rules.md) names in `core` the phrase of the core that carries its obligation for a normal pass, or says in `long_form_only` why a normal pass needs nothing more.
snapshot: 5e0ef0d0 (the integration base the split started from)

bounds.why: Plan U18: the router bound is the plan's 10,000 bytes, which held (the base card's kept sections are 9,475 characters; the route choice and two links bring it to 9,995 bytes). The route bound is set from the measured text, never by trimming an obligation: it holds the policy of four sources (the base card, review-policy.md, callback-evidence.md, ADAPTER.md: 72 KB in all) once each, the handoff's ownership, recovery and return text moved word for word, and the fixed review inputs of improve_prompt (8.3 KB). The plan's first guess for the route was 8,192 bytes. Merged onto INT (U2, U19, U21): the router is 9,977 bytes (U2's shorter description); the route grew to 47,513 bytes because a ShipLoop child now ends each pass with improve-pass, which writes the runtime report from the review file, and the route says so (rows A30, S34); the bound was raised from 46,000 to 48,000, no obligation trimmed. Merged with main's Improve 0.4.4 (upstream Until Loop 0.10.0 vendored byte-identical, 2026-10-18): the lean returns (U21) and the one-unchanged-pass stop rule are dropped, so rows A37 and C33 name the full-return phrase again, A52 is gone with ADAPTER.md's lean-returns block and A15 follows upstream's new head; the route is 47,358 bytes and its bound is now 47,800. The router is 10,271 bytes: main's paragraph on `start --isolated` grew it past 10,000, so its bound was raised to 10,500, no obligation trimmed. Split into a core and case files (2026-10-24, run 4's context measure: the route was read whole 13 times across the run's Improve stages, 629 KB): `route_bytes` now bounds the core, shiploop-route.md, which every ShipLoop child reads, at the plan's 10,000 bytes (measured 9,675); `route_set_bytes` bounds the core and its five case files together (measured 59,077): the old route's text moved there word for word, except its opening paragraph, the review inputs' intro sentence and two sentences the one-pass stop rule (5e377ff7) had left stale (the Exit rule's one-pass Git check, the Assess step's two cycles), and the core restates every every-pass rule as a one-liner. The router is 10,384 bytes: two sentences say the route is a short core.
